# Job Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 421r

---

**1** "We are all born from a woman's womb — our lives are short, and full of trouble.

**2** We spring up like wildflowers, then wilt. We vanish like shadows and cannot hold our ground.

**3** And this is what you fix your eyes on? This is what you drag into court?

**4** Who can bring something pure from something impure? No one can.

**5** Our days are already numbered. You have set the count of our months. You have drawn a line we cannot cross. **6** So look away! Leave us alone! Let us at least have the small satisfaction of a laborer finishing his shift.

**7** Even a tree has more hope than that. If you cut it down, it can still sprout again — its new shoots keep coming. **8** Even if its roots grow old in the ground and its stump seems dead in the dust, **9** the moment it smells water, it buds and puts out branches like a freshly planted sapling.

**10** But when a person dies, that is it. When a human being breathes his last — where has he gone?

**11** Like water disappearing from a lake, like a river that dries up and is gone, **12** so a person lies down and never gets up. Until the sky itself ceases to exist, the dead will not wake. They will not be roused from their sleep.

**13** I wish you would just hide me in the grave! Conceal me there until your anger blows over. Set a date on the calendar and then come back for me!

**14** But if a person dies, can he really live again? I would wait out every day of my hard service if I knew my renewal was coming.

**15** You would call out, and I would answer. You would actually want to see the one you made.

**16** Then you would watch over my steps with care, not keeping a tally of my sins.

**17** My offenses would be sealed up in a pouch, and you would plaster over my guilt.

**18** But no. Mountains collapse and crumble. Boulders shift from their places. **19** Water wears away stone. Floods wash away the soil. And just like that — you wash away every hope a person has.

**20** You overpower us completely, and we are gone. You change our faces and send us away. **21** If our children achieve greatness, we never know. If they suffer, we cannot see it. **22** We feel only our own pain. We mourn only for ourselves."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The great question (v.14):** "If a man dies, shall he live again?" — this is one of the most haunting questions in all of Scripture. Job does not answer it. He allows it to hover, unanswered, over the rest of the book. It is not a statement of faith or a denial of hope — it is the raw question itself, aching for an answer that will not come within these pages.

**The tree and the man (vv.7-12):** The imagery is devastating in its simplicity. A tree — a thing without consciousness, without prayer, without relationship to God — gets what a human being cannot: a second chance. The tree merely needs to "smell" water and it revives. The man sleeps and never wakes. The unfairness is the point.

**Fantasy and collapse (vv.13-19):** Job allows himself a brief fantasy (vv.13-17) — what if God would hide him in Sheol, then remember him? What if God would long for the work of his hands? It is one of the most tender moments in Job. Then vv.18-19 destroy the fantasy: mountains fall, water erodes stone, and God destroys the hope of mortals with the same inevitability. The structure — hope, then the demolition of hope — mirrors Job's own experience.

*— PNEUMA*
